subject: Geography
sub_topic: Major food crops — rice, wheat, pulses

concepts.name: Rice: Agro-Climatic Requirements and Optimal Growing Conditions
key_dimensions: Temperature, rainfall, and soil requirements (clayey loam, kharif crop, 100–200 cm rainfall)
UPSC trap: Rice grown in semi-arid Punjab/Haryana via irrigation — contradiction of natural rainfall requirement
Comparison with wheat requirements to highlight mutual exclusivity of ideal zones
Why rice cultivation leads to groundwater depletion in non-traditional zones (Punjab crisis)

concepts.name: Rice: Major Producing States and Regional Distribution Patterns
key_dimensions: Top producers: West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana — UPSC trap on ranking shifts
West Bengal leads in production but Punjab leads in procurement for PDS — policy vs. geography distinction
North-East India: high rainfall yet low surplus production — subsistence vs. commercial farming contrast
Coastal and delta regions (Krishna-Godavari, Kaveri, Ganga delta) as traditional rice bowls

concepts.name: Green Revolution: Differential Impact on Rice vs. Wheat
key_dimensions: Green Revolution benefited wheat more uniformly; rice gains were concentrated in Punjab, Haryana, AP
HYV seeds: IR-8 for rice vs. Lerma Rojo/Sonalika for wheat — regional adoption disparities
Second Green Revolution concept: extending gains to Eastern India (rice bowl potential of Bihar, WB, Odisha)
UPSC trap: Green Revolution increased production but also increased regional inequality and monoculture risk

concepts.name: Wheat: Agro-Climatic Requirements and Cropping Season
key_dimensions: Rabi crop: cool and dry growing season, warm and dry ripening — precise temperature windows (10–15°C sowing, 21°C ripening)
UPSC trap: wheat requires frost-free conditions at grain-filling stage — late frost is a production risk
Soil preference: well-drained loamy and clayey loam soils of Indo-Gangetic Plain
Comparison: wheat needs moderate rainfall (75–100 cm) or irrigation, unlike rice's waterlogging tolerance

concepts.name: Wheat: Major Producing States and the Indo-Gangetic Plain Dominance
key_dimensions: Top producers: Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan — note MP's rising rank (UPSC trap)
Punjab-Haryana belt: highest productivity per hectare due to irrigation + HYV + MSP incentive combination
Black soil (Deccan) regions grow limited wheat — explains geographical concentration in north
UPSC trap: Uttar Pradesh produces most wheat by volume but Punjab has highest yield per hectare

concepts.name: Minimum Support Price (MSP) and Its Differential Effect on Rice and Wheat vs. Pulses
key_dimensions: MSP announced for 23 crops but effective procurement concentrated in rice and wheat — market distortion
Pulses receive MSP but lack robust procurement infrastructure — UPSC trap on policy vs. implementation gap
MSP for rice and wheat incentivized water-intensive cropping in water-scarce Punjab (environmental trap)
Price Support Scheme (PSS) and Market Intervention Scheme (MIS) as supplementary mechanisms for pulses

concepts.name: Pulses: Botanical Classification, Nutritional Role, and India's Import Dependence
key_dimensions: Pulses as leguminous crops: nitrogen fixation benefit — ecological role distinct from cereals
India: largest producer AND largest consumer AND largest importer of pulses — all three simultaneously (UPSC trap)
Protein security role: pulses as 'poor man's meat' — intersection of nutrition and agricultural policy
Major imported pulses: yellow peas, lentils from Canada/Australia — trade geography angle

concepts.name: Pulses: Major Types, Producing States, and Seasonal Distribution
key_dimensions: Kharif pulses: Tur/Arhar (pigeon pea), Moong, Urad — Maharashtra, Karnataka, UP as top producers
Rabi pulses: Gram/Chana (largest pulse crop by area), Lentil/Masur — MP, Rajasthan dominate
UPSC trap: Gram (chickpea) is the single largest pulse crop in India by both area and production
Madhya Pradesh as the largest pulse-producing state overall — often confused with Maharashtra for Tur

concepts.name: Pulse Productivity Gap: Why India Fails to Achieve Self-Sufficiency
key_dimensions: Pulses grown on marginal, rain-fed, low-fertility lands — structural disadvantage vs. cereals
Lack of HYV adoption at scale and limited irrigation coverage for pulses
UPSC trap: pulses fix nitrogen but are still cultivated on degraded soils — paradox of neglect
Comparison: India's pulse yield (~700 kg/ha) vs. global average (~900 kg/ha) — productivity deficit

concepts.name: Food Security Architecture: Role of Rice and Wheat in PDS and Buffer Stocks
key_dimensions: National Food Security Act (NFSA) 2013: rice at ₹3/kg, wheat at ₹2/kg, coarse grains at ₹1/kg for priority households
Buffer stock norms vs. actual procurement levels — UPSC trap: India often exceeds buffer norms causing storage crisis
Pulses conspicuously absent from NFSA entitlements — policy gap with nutrition implications
FCI's role in rice and wheat procurement vs. NAFED's role in pulses — institutional differentiation

concepts.name: Rice Varieties and Cultivation Practices: SRI, Basmati, and Flood-Tolerant Varieties
key_dimensions: System of Rice Intensification (SRI): less water, less seed, higher yield — contrasts conventional flooded paddy
Basmati rice: GI tag significance, export geography (Haryana, Punjab, UP, Uttarakhand, J&K notified states)
UPSC trap: Swarna Sub-1 (submergence-tolerant variety) — developed for flood-prone Odisha, Bihar, WB
Direct Seeded Rice (DSR) as water-saving alternative to transplanting — Punjab government promotion

concepts.name: Wheat Varieties and the Challenge of Heat Stress Adaptation
key_dimensions: Terminal heat stress: rising March temperatures threatening grain filling in North India
Heat-tolerant varieties: HD 2967, HD 3086, K 0307 — ICAR/CIMMYT collaboration context
UPSC trap: climate change is shifting the wheat-growing calendar and shrinking the ideal cultivation window
Sharbati wheat of MP: premium variety, geographical identity — comparison with Basmati in rice

concepts.name: Crop Rotation and Intercropping Practices Involving Rice, Wheat, and Pulses
key_dimensions: Rice-Wheat cropping system of Indo-Gangetic Plain: dominant but ecologically unsustainable (soil health, water table)
Diversification push: introducing pulses/maize into rice-wheat rotation to restore soil nitrogen
UPSC trap: rice-wheat system covers ~13 million ha in South Asia — policy urgency of diversification
Pulse intercropping with cereals: agro-ecological benefits vs. mechanization challenges

concepts.name: Irrigation Dependency: Contrasting Profiles of Rice, Wheat, and Pulses
key_dimensions: Rice: ~55% of area irrigated; wheat: ~90% of area irrigated — wheat is more irrigation-dependent (UPSC trap)
Pulses: predominantly rain-fed (~85%) — explains yield volatility and price spikes in drought years
Canal vs. groundwater irrigation: Punjab-Haryana shift from canal to tube wells — water table crisis
Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) — 'Har Khet Ko Pani, More Crop Per Drop' relevance

concepts.name: Soil Types and Their Alignment with Major Food Crop Cultivation
key_dimensions: Alluvial soil (Indo-Gangetic Plain): ideal for both rice and wheat — explains regional concentration
Black soil (Regur): suited for cotton and sorghum, not ideal for rice/wheat — UPSC trap on mismatches
Red and laterite soils of peninsular India: support coarse rice varieties, not high-yield wheat
Pulse-soil alignment: gram grows well in black and alluvial soils; arhar prefers red loamy soils

concepts.name: Export-Import Dynamics: Rice as Export Commodity vs. Pulses as Import Commodity
key_dimensions: India is the world's largest rice exporter (non-basmati + basmati combined) — UPSC trap on this dual leadership
2023 rice export ban on non-basmati white rice — food security vs. trade policy tension
Pulses import sources: Canada (lentils), Myanmar (urad/moong), Australia (chickpeas) — geography of dependence
Wheat import history: PL-480 imports from USA (1950s–60s) as historical context for Green Revolution urgency

concepts.name: Government Schemes Specifically Targeting Pulse Production Enhancement
key_dimensions: National Food Security Mission (NFSM) — Pulses component: focus on yield gap reduction in 644 districts
Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA): price support for pulses and oilseeds
UPSC trap: NFSM covers rice, wheat, AND pulses — often candidates think it is only for cereals
Cluster Demonstration approach under NFSM: technology transfer to small/marginal farmers in pulse belts

concepts.name: Climate Change Vulnerabilities: Differential Risks for Rice, Wheat, and Pulses
key_dimensions: Rice: methane emissions from flooded paddy fields — agriculture's contribution to GHG (UPSC intersection with environment)
Wheat: most vulnerable to temperature rise — 1°C increase projected to reduce yield by 6–7% in South Asia
Pulses: erratic monsoon = high price volatility; but also most climate-resilient in terms of water needs
UPSC trap: elevated CO₂ may boost photosynthesis but increased temperatures simultaneously reduce yields — net negative for cereals

concepts.name: Nutritional Security Dimension: Shifting from Calorie-Centric (Rice/Wheat) to Protein-Inclusive (Pulses) Policy
key_dimensions: India's hidden hunger: calorie adequate but protein/micronutrient deficient — PDS bias toward rice/wheat
National Nutrition Mission (POSHAN Abhiyaan) and the case for pulse inclusion in midday meal schemes
UPSC trap: India's per capita pulse availability has declined from ~60g/day (1960s) to ~35g/day (2020s) despite production growth
Biofortified varieties: iron-rich pearl millet, protein-rich chickpea — intersection of agriculture and health policy

concepts.name: Geographical Indications (GI) Tags for Food Crops: Rice and Pulse Varieties
key_dimensions: Basmati rice GI tag: 7 states notified, ongoing India-Pakistan dispute at international level (UPSC current affairs trap)
Govind Bhog rice (WB), Kalanamak rice (UP), Pokkali rice (Kerala) — state-specific GI-tagged rice varieties
UPSC trap: Pokkali rice is a saline-tolerant traditional variety — climate resilience + GI tag dual significance
Pulse GI examples: limited currently — contrast with rice to highlight policy attention disparity
